name: Brussels
title: Holidays in Brussels
intro: Europe's capital, with a gilded medieval square, art nouveau houses, comic-strip murals and the world's best chips, waffles and chocolate. Here's what Brussels is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The ornate guild houses of the Grand-Place in Brussels with crowds in the square
facts_note: The Eurostar from London takes about 2 hours. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to June and September are best for walking the city. In mid August of even-numbered years the Grand-Place is covered in a flower carpet. December brings the Winter Wonders market and lights. Rain is common at any time of year.

things.name: Grand-Place
things.blurb: One of Europe's finest squares, ringed by gilded guild houses. Lovely lit up at night.

things.name: Manneken Pis
things.blurb: The tiny statue of a boy, often dressed in one of his hundreds of costumes.

things.name: Atomium
things.blurb: A giant model of an iron crystal from the 1958 World's Fair, with a viewing sphere.

things.name: Comic strip trail
things.blurb: Murals of Tintin and other comic heroes painted on walls around the city.

things.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts and Magritte Museum
things.blurb: Flemish masters and the world's biggest Magritte collection.

things.name: Bruges or Ghent
things.blurb: Both medieval canal towns are under an hour by train.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Brussels?
faqs.answer: Two days covers the city. Add a day for Bruges, Ghent or Antwerp.

faqs.question: How do you get to Brussels from London?
faqs.answer: The Eurostar from St Pancras takes about 2 hours to Brussels-Midi.

faqs.question: What food is Brussels famous for?
faqs.answer: Frites with mayonnaise, waffles, chocolate, mussels and a huge range of Belgian beers.

faqs.question: Is Brussels expensive?
faqs.answer: It's mid-priced for a European capital. Hotels are cheaper at weekends, when EU business travel drops.
